speaker: m_ana
text: Mom's seventy-eight and alone in Queens. She mixes up her pills, she almost wired money to someone pretending to be Marco last week, and last Thursday nobody went to see her because Marco and I each thought the other was going.

speaker: m_ana
text: Marco and me, and our sister Lucía in New Jersey. Marco's in Astoria, ten minutes from Mom. I'm in Brooklyn, forty minutes. Lucía can't come on short notice, but she does the refills and the insurance calls.
asked: Who else is in this besides you and Marco, and where does everyone live relative to your mom?

speaker: m_ana
text: He works nights. Sunday to Thursday he has to leave by nine-thirty. He sleeps until two in the afternoon. He can do Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings. He wants a text at three on his days so he doesn't forget.
asked: What is Marco's week like? When can he actually be there?

speaker: m_ana
text: Monday, Wednesday, Sunday, after four. I do all the doctor visits. Sunday lunch is at Mom's and I fill her pill organizer then.

speaker: m_ana
text: Eliquis morning and night. Lisinopril in the morning, which Dr. Park just doubled to ten milligrams on the third. Metformin twice a day. Atorvastatin at night. The old lisinopril bottle is still in her cabinet, that scares me. Farmacia La Esquina on 37th fills everything.
asked: Her pills: what does she take, and who prescribed them?

speaker: m_ana
text: Weekly organizer, yellow lid for morning, blue lid for evening. Two or three nights a week she calls me asking if she took them. Once she took them twice.
asked: How does she take them, and what happens on the nights she isn't sure?

speaker: m_ana
text: Someone called saying he was Marco, crying, in trouble, needed fifteen hundred dollars in gift cards. She was on her way to the store when Marco happened to call her. Marco handles her money stuff with her. She has one checking account and that's it.
asked: Money. Tell me about the call last week.

speaker: m_ana
text: Pavo. Thanksgiving is at her place and Marco always brings the turkey.
asked: Pick a word only the family knows. Every real call from Village says it, so a caller without it is not us.

speaker: m_ana
text: Breakfast at eight with the morning pills. Blood pressure Monday, Wednesday, Friday, she writes it on a pad. Walk to the bakery at eleven with Doña Rosa, her neighbor on the third floor. Dinner at seven with her telenovela, evening pills at seven-thirty. It's a second-floor walk-up, no elevator; the super is Luis.
asked: Her day and her home: what does a normal day look like, and is anyone nearby?

speaker: m_ana
text: 911, then me, then Marco. Elmhurst Hospital.
asked: If she falls or can't breathe, who is first?

speaker: m_ana
text: Spanish only. A regular phone, she won't use apps. Big letters if anything. She'll answer a call; she won't read a text.
asked: Her phone and her language: what will she actually use?

speaker: m_ana
text: After lunch, around one-thirty. And she hates calls at night.
asked: Two things Village can't take from you: Lucía's own yes to being called, and your mom's rules. Village asks Lucía in her app and calls your mom in Spanish to introduce itself. She can say no to all of it. When is she sharpest?

speaker: m_ana
text: Lucía should see the refill list too, she does the ordering.
asked: Here is the draft: four people, three life areas, five needs, ten rules on, one thing pending your mom. What is wrong?
